claims.explanation: Bergenin's anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, particularly its inhibition of TNF-α and IL-1β signaling and activation of PPARγ, may sensitize cancer cells with high basal NF-κB activity or dependence on inflammatory cytokines. Conversely, intact KEAP1/NRF2-mediated antioxidant responses or high SIRT1 expression could protect cells by counteracting bergenin's pro-oxidant effects. The selective killing pattern suggests that tumors with mutations in chromatin modifiers or DNA repair genes may be more vulnerable due to impaired stress responses.

features.basis: KEAP1 mutations activate NRF2, enhancing antioxidant capacity and likely reducing bergenin's oxidative stress
NRF2 activation increases antioxidant enzymes, counteracting bergenin's pro-oxidant effects
Bergenin acts via PPARγ to increase SIRT1; high SIRT1 may protect by inhibiting NF-κB
Bergenin is a PPARγ agonist; high PPARγ may mediate anti-inflammatory and anti-proliferative effects
Bergenin inhibits TNF-α; tumors with high TNF-α signaling may be more dependent and thus sensitive
Bergenin inhibits IL-1β; tumors with high IL-1β signaling may be more sensitive
Bergenin inhibits NF-κB; tumors with high NF-κB activity may be more dependent and sensitive
TP53 mutations are common in sensitive lines; loss of p53 may impair antioxidant response
STK11 mutations observed in several sensitive lines; may impair AMPK-mediated stress resistance
BRAF mutations in sensitive melanoma lines; may indicate MAPK pathway dependence
PIK3CA mutations in sensitive lines; may indicate PI3K/AKT dependence
PTEN mutations in resistant lines; loss may activate survival pathways
